entries.summary: Added a live credential verification check before every mode opens, with a blocking gate if your LLM API key is missing or expired. Previously, a present-but-expired key would silently walk into the fallback path and generate misleading content (action items that say 'Address: <topic>' with no explanation). Now every mode verifies the credential works before starting, distinguishing between a definite rejection and inconclusive network errors (so it won't block on a captive wifi). Usage and Settings modes are exempt because they make no LLM calls. The check is also skipped with --dry-run, which is used by the demo recorder and test suite.

highlights.text: Live LLM credential verification: before any mode opens, ping the API to confirm your key is valid and your subscription is active
Blocking gate on invalid API keys: stops confusing AI-generated fallback content from appearing when credentials are missing or expired
Smart network error handling: distinguishes between a definite credential rejection and transient network issues (captive wifi, proxy) so it won't over-block
Per-mode exemptions: Usage (local dashboard) and Settings (credential management) don't gate on LLM availability since they don't call the API

entries.summary: Hardened the Cloudflare tunnel sharing path with an opt-in verified-users tier (YEABOI_SHARE_MODE=access). The quick-tunnel default now uses the real visitor IP for rate limiting instead of collapsing into one bucket, refused holds back off server-side, and the cloudflared binary is verified on every launch. The new access tier adds a named tunnel with verified identity: local JWT verification with RS256 keys, hostname claim registry, server-side impersonation prevention on retro/poker/share/ship surfaces, and a four-step setup wizard integrated into Settings. Cloudflared is now containerized with an allowlisted environment (no API keys, pinned logging and metrics), and tunnel hostname redaction from logs keeps host metadata private.

highlights.text: New verified-users access tier (opt-in via YEABOI_SHARE_MODE=access): named tunnel with JWT identity verification and server-side impersonation checks
Quick-tunnel default improvements: real visitor IP for rate limiting, refused holds back off server-side, binary digest verified on each launch
Sharing is now a dedicated Settings tab with one-time setup wizard: domain, Access app creation, and team/AUD auto-detection
Cloudflared containment: child process gets allowlisted environment (no API keys), pinned logging, isolated session, hostname redacted from all logs
Server-side identity verification on all tunnel surfaces (retro, poker, share, ship) prevents bearer-token and admin-flag impersonation

entries.summary: Slack integration is now two-way: reactions and replies on ceremony posts control ceremonies, vote on practice signals, and correct artifacts. With both SLACK_BOT_TOKEN and SLACK_CHANNEL_ID configured, ceremony delivery posts via chat.postMessage and records an anchor row, while a background polling job reads the channel every N minutes and applies what it finds. Four acts exist: emoji reactions on the post control pause/resume/skip, vote reactions on signal replies apply verdicts, short text replies (pause/resume/skip/ack) call the same store functions, and any other threaded reply becomes an attributed correction. All four acts are free, reversible database writes with no LLM anywhere in the inbound path, and the allowlist is empty by default (making the poll a no-op). The Slack column moved from the Ceremonies page to a page-level fact line, showing post status, channel, and token/reader configuration. A one-shot ceremony skip flag and artifact leases for concurrent edits round out the delivery improvements.

highlights.text: Reactions and replies on Slack posts now control ceremonies: ⏸ ▶️ 🚫 on the post pause/resume/skip; 👍/👎 on signal replies cast verdicts
Short text replies (pause/resume/skip/ack) execute store calls; any other reply becomes an attributed correction
Background polling job reads the channel every N minutes and applies reactions/replies as database writes, with no LLM in the path
SLACK_ALLOWED_MEMBER_IDS allowlist gates who can react; empty list disables the poll entirely
One-shot ceremony skip via Ceremony.skip_next ISO date flag; artifact leases prevent concurrent edits during votes

entries.summary: The poker and retro live boards have been redesigned on a shared component kit with a unified design system. The new design introduces an elevation ladder, radius and motion scales, and vendored icon set that powers both boards. Retro cards are now draggable with GPU-accelerated transforms, reactions are displayed as a glass tray, and the facilitator controls moved to a right rail with real history of past retros and AI-powered action-item suggestions. Poker gained a dynamic duel experience with proper turn announcement, an improved table layout, and the duck mascot that responds to game events. Both boards now survive small windows down to 16px and share a unified toolbar and room roster.

highlights.text: Retro cards are now draggable with GPU-accelerated transforms and glass-tray reactions
Facilitator rail shows retro history and provides admin-gated AI action-item suggestions
Poker duel experience redesigned with proper turn announcement and improved table layout
Unified design system shared between poker and retro: elevation ladder, motion scales, and shared icon set
Both boards now survive small windows and adapt gracefully on mobile devices

entries.summary: yeaboi now supports Claude subscription authentication using long-lived OAuth tokens instead of just API keys. The settings page gains a new auth-mode row where you can choose between API key and subscription token, and a seamless in-app setup flow — `claude setup-token` runs interactively on a managed pty while you stay in the TUI, letting you authorize in a browser and paste the code without leaving the app. Tokens are monitored for staleness via a free probe at launch, and if one expires during use, the duck alerts you with a Ctrl+R shortcut to refresh. The implementation includes new guardrails for OAuth beta compatibility, token extraction from CLI output, and a new provider card in the setup wizard.

highlights.text: Choose between API key and subscription token in settings — new auth-mode row with derived provider list and credentials UI
Sign in with `claude setup-token` without leaving the app — runs the CLI on a managed pty, opens a browser, and stays in the TUI throughout
Subscription tokens are validated at launch via a free probe and monitored for staleness, with Ctrl+R to refresh when needed
Full OAuth 2025-04-20 beta support with Bearer token auth instead of API key headers

entries.summary: Ship mode now surfaces a live, shareable web board — teammates can watch the story→PR pipeline run in real time over a browser, including the five-phase checklist, live agent activity, the diff, validation results, and cost estimates. The board is read-only for this release; guests watch from any device via a Cloudflare tunnel while you drive approval/rejection from the TUI. The board reuses the existing retro/poker live-board infrastructure and security model. Additionally, ship mode fixes a critical plan-finding bug where plans saved in the interactive planning chat were invisible ("no stories found") and adds cloud-friendly Cloudflare tunnel option for remote team collaboration.

highlights.text: Live ship board shows the five-phase checklist, agent activity, diff, validation results, and cost in real-time over the browser
Share the board with teammates over a Cloudflare tunnel — read-only guests watch the run while you drive from the TUI
Ship mode now finds plans saved in both the interactive planning chat and the project store, fixing the "no stories found" bug on chat-built plans
Live agent output streams over the TUI and the web board via stream-json format with hardened envelope parsing

entries.summary: yeaboi now runs on a clock. Ceremonies let you schedule any of six catalogued modes — standup, report, and four agentwatch digests — to fire at a specific time on weekdays and deliver results to Slack, email, or terminal while yeaboi is closed. The OS installs the job (launchd on macOS, cron elsewhere); yeaboi's scheduler catches its fire, runs the engine, records the outcome and cost in a ledger, and applies three guards that block stale fires, cap spending, or respect pauses. You declare a ceremony once, and it runs unattended every week. The ceremony CLI lives under `yeaboi ceremonies` (add/list/remove/pause/resume/run/history/modes), with a dedicated TUI page for viewing schedules, pausing runs, and seeing OS/store drift.

highlights.text: Schedule any mode to run at a time on weekdays with `yeaboi ceremonies add` — standup, report, and agentwatch digests deliver to Slack, email, or terminal
OS-installed jobs (launchd/cron) fire ceremonies while yeaboi is closed, with each run recorded in a ledger showing outcome, duration, cost, and delivery status
Three guards protect unattended runs: staleness rejects fires too late for their slot, spending caps prevent budget overruns, and pause status gates fires
New TUI page shows your ceremony schedule, lets you run or pause them, and displays any drift between the store and the OS
Delivery was unified onto a mode-neutral Dispatch type, reducing code duplication and making new delivery channels easier to add

entries.summary: The standup now shows an activity timeline swimlane board with landmarks and thread connections, while Azure DevOps PR reviews are captured and properly deduplicated. Four bugs in the Azure DevOps integration are fixed: reviewer votes were not fetched, comments incorrectly collapsed to one row per PR, activity caps silently dropped events, and the capability manifest claimed the opposite of reality. The standup timeline redesign replaces mute tick marks with labeled landmarks (merged PRs, ticket state changes) and commit bursts, using a compressed axis where events claim footprints and overlapping activity merges into bursts. Threads now connect lanes that touched the same pull request, and evidence caps widened from 8 to 30 rows per category to support busier days.

highlights.text: Standup timeline visualizes activity as labeled landmarks and commit bursts on a compressed axis with thread connections between PRs
Azure DevOps PR reviewer votes are now captured and appear in standup evidence
Azure DevOps PR comments no longer incorrectly collapse to a single row per PR
Evidence caps per category widened from 8 to 30 to support busier days without silent truncation
Activity timeline geometry invariants tested across zoom levels, themes, and single vs. multi-day boards

entries.summary: Ship mode hardening and safety improvements prevent agent capability creep, tighten consent checks, and show you the exact changes before approval. The agent's Bash tool is now completely denied (not just git/gh commands), closing permission-bypass risks from other shell features. Consent is checked against the git toplevel where worktree setup actually lands, so approval names the directory that is actually touched. The approval gate now renders a scrollable patch pane showing your complete diff alongside validation results, with measured button positioning that never leaves buttons off-screen on minimum terminals. Gates answer only their own run by capturing the run id immediately, preventing concurrent runs from presenting stale diffs to the wrong user. Run IDs now carry a random suffix preventing same-second collisions, and removal operations report correctly whether they found an entry.

highlights.text: Agent permissions hardened: Bash tool is completely denied, not just git/gh commands, closing permission bypasses
Consent checks the git toplevel, so approval dialog names the exact directory that is touched
Approval gate shows the full diff in a scrollable patch pane with validation results and the worktree path
The approval buttons always stay on screen, however long the diff or failure log; supporting detail yields space first
Gates answer only their own run via immediate run-id callback; concurrent runs no longer see stale diffs

entries.summary: Wave 6 of the Go migration brings the documentation quality scoring engine behind the yeaboi-core sidecar. The analysis module now scores documentation clarity, AI usage patterns, and content quality in the background Go service with Python fallback, running ~100x faster than the Python implementation. Two new deterministic RPC methods enable the analysis pipeline to classify content markers and score documentation across your team's work without blocking the standup or analysis runs. Parity tests enforce byte-level equivalence across Python and Go implementations, and contract definitions lock the RPC interface across versions. This completes the deterministic scoring seam that began with Wave 5 (code health and practices).

highlights.text: Doc quality scoring now runs in the Go sidecar with two new RPC methods: score_docs and classify_doc_markers
~100x faster documentation scoring: Go implementation replaces Python read workers, cache writes batch at the seam
Byte-level parity enforcement ensures Python and Go doc-quality implementations stay perfectly synchronized
Silent Python fallback preserves compatibility when the sidecar is unavailable or encounters errors
Completes the deterministic scoring seam: doc quality joins code health and practices in the Go backend

entries.summary: The Ship mode closes yeaboi's feedback loop: a user story from your saved sprint plan is handed to a supervised Claude Code headless agent in an isolated git worktree, its diff is validated deterministically, a human approves it at a gate, and only then is the branch pushed and a PR opened. Features include a global budget fuse with quota tracking and fail-closed safety, a worktree coordinator that handles repo setup and cleanup, a mechanical driver that strips agent permissions (no git push, no command execution), and a pipeline with precondition validation and 3-attempt reviewer gates.

highlights.text: Ship mode: deliver user stories directly from sprint plan via supervised coding agent in isolated worktree
Budget fuse: user-global quota (1 concurrent / 2 per hour / 12 per day) with fail-closed safety and circuit breaker on quota errors
Deterministic gate: validation runs in its own process, precondition checks for empty diffs, and reviewer can request rework with feedback
Mechanical safety: agent cannot run git or shell commands; only yeaboi commits and pushes after approval
Full surfaces: TUI beta card with picker/progress/gate/result screens, CLI commands (run/status/history), MCP tools, and plugin skill

entries.summary: Planning mode's prior-art intake flow now batches all candidate repos into a single multi-select carousel instead of asking about each one individually. Select multiple repos at once with Space, navigate with arrow keys, and use X to permanently dismiss a candidate. Rejections no longer blacklist repos globally — unchecking just skips them for this project, while X explicitly bans them forever. The new batch grammar works everywhere: TUI carousel, CLI flags, headless APIs, and REPL forms all use the same syntax (numbers, ranges, all, none, or !N bans). Resume now correctly replays the batch prompt instead of stale hints.

highlights.text: Batch multi-select carousel for prior-art intake: select all relevant repos at once instead of one-by-one confirmation
Kinder rejection semantics: unchecked repos are skipped for this project only; explicit X bans them permanently
Unified batch grammar works on all surfaces: TUI, CLI, headless, and REPL use consistent 1/3, all, none, !N syntax
Fixed resume flow to replay the batch prompt correctly instead of stale hints

entries.summary: Deterministic signals now carry a tamper-evident, auditable decision chain that tracks the evidence behind every verdict. Provenance adds a new run_provenance_audit engine and command-line tools to verify chain integrity and trace any signal to the data that produced it. Standup surfaces conflicts as explicit cards when sources disagree (board says Done but a PR is open), and every standup decision (practice signals, confidence verdicts, LLM-adjudication drops) chains its evidence. Performance mode's 1:1 preps, completions, and reviews record their source ticket keys so every assessment is traceable. Payloads carry severity as a word, resolution strategies default to manual review, and failed chain writes become report warnings instead of blocking runs. New provenance audit|trace CLI commands and MCP tools bring full parity to headless and agent-driven workflows.

highlights.text: Tamper-evident decision chain: hash-chained append-only log verifies that every decision is unedited and can be traced to its source
Conflict detection surfaces disagreements as cards: board says Done but a PR is open, confidence is adjusting due to conflicting signals
Every standup decision now chains its evidence: practice signals and their verdicts, confidence adjustments and their reasons, LLM-adjudication drops
Performance 1:1s and reviews record source ticket keys so every assessment is tied to its source data
New `yeaboi provenance audit|trace` CLI commands and MCP tools expose full chain verification to headless and agent workflows

entries.summary: Planning mode gained five major capabilities: sprint targeting for small projects (reuse existing sprints and assign stories without creating new ones), team-style acceptance criteria with learned and customizable formats, architecture options with opt-in validation spikes (2–3 options with confidence scoring), and PRD export for full product requirements documents. Tracker sync fixes kill the Sprint -1 bug and add full pagination, closed-sprint safety, and ISO-8601 datetime handling. The story writer and all renderers now follow learned team acceptance-criteria styles, and custom Definition-of-Done lists are normalized and honored in every sync path.

highlights.text: Small projects can now target existing sprints, assigning stories without creating new ones
Team-style acceptance criteria: learned formats (GWT, free text) drive story writer and every exporter with custom DoD support
Architecture options phase proposes 2–3 validated alternatives with pros/cons and honest confidence scoring
Opt-in validation spike: user confirms recommendations; spike story auto-pinned to Sprint 1 (large) or first spike task (small) with deterministic sizing
PRD export: full Product Requirements Document with MVP scope, team's AC style, architecture, phased sprints, and risks — one LLM call with deterministic fallback
Tracker sync overhaul: Sprint -1 bug fixed, boards fully paginated, closed sprints never targeted, ISO-8601 datetimes with non-overlapping inclusive ends

entries.summary: The Agent Advisor joins the Agents family as the fourth agentwatch mode, turning the cost meter into a cost advisor that answers "how much of what my agents cost was avoidable, and why". The mode audits waste in your local agent transcripts — re-reads, subset reads, write read-backs, and stale reads — priced at your actual blended cache-aware rate, and surfaces structural markers of cache volatility in CLAUDE.md prefixes (UUIDs, timestamps, JWTs) that cause premature cache evictions. Full surface parity brings the advisor to the TUI as a new Advisor card and page, CLI `yeaboi agents advisor`, MCP tools for RPC-driven analysis, and a plugin skill for AI-assistant integration. Privacy is preserved: transcripts and prefix files are read locally; only counts, totals and file paths reach the artifact and database.

highlights.text: New Agent Advisor mode audits recoverable spend in local Claude Code transcripts with honest pricing at your blended cache rate
Waste detection catches re-reads, subset re-reads, write read-backs, and stale reads with deterministic mechanism fixtures
Cache health scoring detects volatile content in CLAUDE.md prefixes (UUIDs, timestamps, JWTs) that cause premature evictions
Full surface parity: TUI Advisor card and page, CLI subcommand, MCP tools, and Claude Code plugin skill
Privacy preserved: transcripts and prefix files read locally; only counts, totals and paths reach artifacts and storage

entries.summary: Faster, more reliable release pipeline with internal improvements to the fleet feedback loop and verification gate. The ship gate now runs 2.5× faster (full test suite in 120s instead of 289s) by parallelizing unit tests, and it verifies the correct tree by fetching before rebase. The fleet gained a feedback system that records every rejection reason for calibration, hygiene lenses to surface high-impact sweeps, and self-tightening rules that make the fleet quieter without human intervention. No user-facing feature changes.

highlights.text: Ship gate now runs 2.5× faster with parallelized unit tests (120s instead of 289s), correctly verifying the merge target tree
Fleet feedback loop records rejection reasons for calibration and surfaces high-impact opportunities via hygiene lenses
Hygiene lenses provide objective criteria for fleet self-improvement without requiring human oversight

entries.summary: The agent standup digest now reports what it actually measured instead of what it happened to find. When it runs somewhere with no access to your local agent history, it can be told to skip collecting sessions entirely rather than scanning and counting itself, and it says plainly that sessions were not collected. A digest with no sessions no longer prints a $0.00 total, which read as “the agents were free today” when it meant “that is not what this run measured” — the terminal, the shared file and the chat post now all lead with the same honest headline. Session highlights describe what an agent did rather than simply listing the most expensive session.

highlights.text: The agent standup can now skip local session collection, so a digest run away from your machine no longer counts itself as the day’s only agent
A digest with no sessions reports what it did measure instead of a $0.00 total that read as free
Session highlights now say what an agent worked on rather than ranking sessions by cost

entries.summary: Fixed a silent data loss bug in the Notion integration where pages with more than 100 top-level blocks were truncated without notification. The tool now paginates through all child blocks until completion or a resource ceiling, and reports every partial read with a truncation marker so the LLM knows the document it read was incomplete.

highlights.text: Notion page reads now paginate through all child blocks (was truncating after 100 blocks silently)
All partial reads are now reported with a truncation marker so incomplete documents are visible

entries.summary: When starting a greenfield project in Planning mode, yeaboi now offers your team's own repositories as prior art — ranked by relevance to the project requirements and presented with a concrete pitch of what each repo does. This leverages the team inventory that Team Analysis already fetches, so no new API calls are needed. Accepted prior-art repositories feed into plan generation and appear in the summary and exports. Rejections are remembered globally with the user's reason, so irrelevant repos are never re-offered. The step sits between the PTO sub-loop and the intake summary, and degrades gracefully to deterministic fallback facts if the LLM fails.

highlights.text: Greenfield planning now ranks your team's existing repositories and offers the relevant ones as prior art with concrete pitches
Accepted prior-art repos feed plan generation and appear in the summary and exports for full context
Rejections are remembered globally with user reasons — irrelevant repos are never re-offered across sessions
Prior-art step degrades gracefully to deterministic ranking fallback if the LLM is unavailable

entries.summary: GitHub configuration now gets its own dedicated picker flow in Daily Standup's Configure screen, replacing the combined GitHub/Azure DevOps interface. When you pick GitHub organizations, a second screen lists every repository in those organizations with a repo-exclude interface — all repos are pre-checked by default, and you only untick the ones to exclude. This opt-out model means newly created repos are scanned automatically without reconfiguration. The owner picker now correctly pre-selects all discovered organizations when GitHub is added to a standup previously configured for Azure DevOps only. Beyond the UI, the configuration now includes a new `github_excluded_repositories` field (schema v29), threaded through the store, engine, collector, MCP tools, and CLI. Setup and token documentation has been clarified: the GITHUB_TOKEN requires both the 'repo' scope and SSO authorization if your organization mandates it — both requirements are now documented in the setup wizard, Settings, and .env.example.

highlights.text: GitHub organizations now have their own picker and dedicated repo-exclude screen instead of sharing space with Azure DevOps
Repo-exclude interface lists all discovered repos pre-checked — untick only what you want to exclude, new repos are scanned automatically
Fixed owner picker pre-selection when adding GitHub to a standup previously configured for Azure DevOps only — now correctly pre-ticks all discovered GitHub orgs
GITHUB_TOKEN scope and SSO requirements now clearly documented in setup wizard, Settings, and .env.example to prevent configuration errors
New CLI flag --github-excluded-repositories and MCP tool support for repository exclusion management

entries.summary: Cloudflare share tunnels now auto-expire with a configurable timeout to prevent accidentally leaving boards or shares internet-reachable indefinitely. By default, every retro board, planning poker session, and anonymized or editable share closes automatically 60 minutes after it opens. The timeout is adjustable via the new TUNNEL_TIMEOUT_MINUTES environment variable (any positive integer for minutes, or 0 to disable auto-expiry entirely), and surfaced on the TUI's Settings > System page for point-and-click configuration. Enforcement happens inside the CloudflareTunnel class itself with a background timer that fires only if the tunnel stays open — manual stop() cancels the timer. When a tunnel expires, retro and poker boards fall back to their existing "Retry Link" failure state, while output shares collapse to "Back only" with the expiry message.

highlights.text: Share tunnels auto-expire 60 minutes after opening by default, preventing accidentally left-open boards
Configurable via TUNNEL_TIMEOUT_MINUTES env var or new Settings > System page row; set to 0 to disable auto-expiry
Retro/poker boards fall back to "Retry Link" state; shares collapse to "Back only" with expiry notice
Background timer runs only while tunnel is open and is safely cancelled on manual stop()

entries.summary: Fixed critical paste handling defects in the chat box that corrupted input and broke keyboard ergonomics. Pasted text larger than 10,000 characters now drains fully and stays within the cap instead of overflowing into the tty as keystrokes; newlines are preserved across platforms (Windows CRLF, Unix LF, old Mac CR); UTF-8 characters no longer decode as replacement characters; and escape sequences in the read-ahead tail no longer phantom-quit the chat. The newline key hint was corrected: Ctrl+N has always worked but was invisible, while the advertised Alt+Enter needs iTerm2/Terminal.app configuration that many users don't have. The hint row is now dynamic, dropping lower-priority hints by segment rather than ellipsizing mid-word on narrow terminals. Ctrl+U now clearly indicates what it does and remembers the previous draft for one Ctrl+U press, so you can undo a clear without re-typing. All changes are keyboard ergonomics only — no new user-facing features.

highlights.text: Paste handling fixed: oversized pastes drain to 10,000 characters (not spilling as keystrokes), newlines preserved across platforms, UTF-8 decodes correctly, no character corruption
Newline key now clearly advertises Ctrl+N (always worked, now visible) over Alt+Enter (which needs terminal config)
Hint row now drops lower-priority segments instead of ellipsizing mid-word on narrow terminals, keeping the essential hints visible
Ctrl+U shows what it does and restores the previous draft on the next Ctrl+U, so you can undo a clear without re-typing
Fixed: escape sequences in the read-ahead buffer no longer phantom-quit the chat and type literal characters

entries.summary: Daily Standup now offers GitHub organization-level scoping, bringing it to feature parity with Azure DevOps project selection. Instead of manually ticking individual repositories, you can now pick GitHub organisations in Configure → Code Sources, and the standup automatically discovers and tracks all repositories within those organisations. The picker intelligently expands owners per run (not at configure time), so newly created repositories are immediately available without any reconfiguration. Repository discovery is capped at the 10 most recently pushed per owner to keep the collector efficient, and GitHub API errors are handled gracefully as warnings rather than blocking the entire source.

highlights.text: GitHub organizations now appear in the code sources picker alongside Azure DevOps projects
Organizations expand per run to discover repositories automatically, including newly created repos without reconfiguration
Repository discovery is capped at 10 per owner and 30 total to prevent bottlenecking the standup's 10-minute run window
New github_owners CLI flag and MCP tool parameter brings feature parity across all surfaces

entries.summary: Daily Standup fixes two critical reachability defects: the browser-editable share now appears on live pages (not just saved runs), and skipped sources are now named with reasons in the progress steps, TUI panels, and broadcast surfaces. A new Sources action lets you reconfigure code sources on any standup page after initial setup. GitHub API errors (403/404/rate-limit) are now safely caught per-source, and one vocabulary bridges source labels across four surfaces — no more mismatches between "GitHub" and "GitHub code" between the report and progress steps.

highlights.text: Live standup pages now have an editable share like saved runs, with the same edit-log replay and attribution tracking
Skipped sources now appear everywhere: progress steps name each skipped source and its reason (not selected, no credentials, empty scope)
New Sources action allows post-setup reconfiguration of code sources (GitHub, Azure Repos, Local Git, Confluence, Notion)
GitHub API errors are now safely caught per-source with verbose logging, preventing one unreachable repo from blocking the rest
Unified source vocabulary: source_label bridges progress steps, TUI, web exports, and broadcast surfaces — consistent naming across all surfaces

entries.summary: Wave 5 of the Go migration brings the team-analysis scoring core (code health evaluation, coverage assessment, and code practice classification) behind the yeaboi-core sidecar. Two new deterministic RPC methods enable the analysis module to classify code markers and score repository health in the background Go service with Python fallback. The seam carefully orchestrates concurrent LLM work and file-fetch operations for optimal performance. Parity tests enforce byte-level equivalence across Python and Go implementations, and contract definitions lock the RPC interface across versions.

highlights.text: Analysis scoring core now runs in the Go sidecar with two new RPC methods: classify_markers and score_code
New aggregate module coordinates concurrent analysis work (LLM classification + network file fetches) with optimal parallelism
Byte-level parity enforcement for analysis module ensures Python and Go implementations stay perfectly synchronized
Silent Python fallback preserves compatibility when the sidecar is unavailable or encounters errors

entries.summary: The Go migration begins with the yeaboi-core sidecar now serving the deterministic agentwatch and standup engines. Platform wheels ship automatically with the `yeaboi[core]` extra, and the binary is auto-detected at runtime with silent Python fallback. Agentwatch scans are now ~30× faster (15–30s → ~1.1s), CLI startup is ~16× faster (0.65s → 0.04s), and the standup.aggregate RPC delivers deterministic report composition with byte-level contract enforcement. The migration is transparent — no breaking changes, no new CLI flags, no TUI changes. Python remains the reference implementation; Go and Python stay synchronized via parity tests covering every output byte.

highlights.text: Go sidecar binary (yeaboi-core) now serves agentwatch and standup deterministic engines with ~30× faster scans and ~16× faster CLI startup
Platform wheels for yeaboi-core (macOS Intel/Apple, Linux x86_64/ARM64, Windows) ship via `yeaboi[core]` extra with auto-detection at runtime
Transparent sidecar migration with silent Python fallback — no user-facing changes, full backward compatibility
Byte-level parity tests ensure Python and Go remain synchronized on every engine output

entries.summary: The Agents family (Usage, Standup, Security) now ships with full website and documentation coverage. All three agent modes appear in the new docs structure with pages explaining what each tracks and how to use them. The demo now tours the split landing screen, both the Humans and Agents menus, and the complete agent mode interface — deterministic, fully verified, and working. Across the entire project, the tagline evolved from "A team lead's best friend" to "Best friend to engineers and agents," appearing consistently in the README, CLI banner, package metadata, MCP instructions, website, all 23 documentation pages, and the plugin marketplace manifest, while keeping "AI Scrum Master" as the core SEO term in the title and badge.

highlights.text: Complete Agents family documentation: three new pages (index, usage, standup, security) in the docs site
Demo fixed and rebuilt: tours Humans/Agents split, both mode menus, and the complete agent interface in 19 seconds, synced on screen markers
Tagline updated across all surfaces: README, CLI, package metadata, website, MCP, docs, and plugin marketplace manifest
Website hero rebuilt with all three landing screens (split, Humans menu, Agents menu) and scrolly-rail navigation
Fixed latent race in screen marker detection and mobile split sizing with button font inheritance

entries.summary: Standup output is now significantly cleaner across all surfaces — web page, markdown exports, Slack, and email. Facts are shown once instead of being repeated 3–4 times, quiet team members collapse into a single summary line, and vanity stats are removed from view. The engine dedupes by category and by ticket key, while presentation layers strip redundant explanations. Sync commits and PR merge pairs are consolidated into single evidence rows. Automation notices are now grouped compactly instead of scattered. On average, a 6-member standup report shrinks from 99 dense lines to 75 clean ones.

highlights.text: Each fact now appears once — category prose suppressed when structured evidence rows exist, member summaries dedupe per ticket key
Zero-activity members collapse into a single "No activity detected" row across web, markdown, Slack, and email
Vanity footnotes and stat tiles removed; coverage is stated once in the Details section
Merge commit pairs and sync commits deduplicated; PR-bypassing and thin commits excluded from evidence
Automation exclusion notices grouped compactly per cluster; cleaner, more readable reports overall

entries.summary: The agent pages (Usage, Standup, Security) now load with clear progress feedback instead of a firehose of transcript lines. Phase-based checklist loading screens show what's happening (scan/price/insights) with a percentage meter and elapsed time, while the last saved report opens instantly and updates in the background. A refresh banner shows the running phase and progress so you always know the page is working, and background progress is streamed and folded into one compact meter instead of spamming the display. Stale reports stay visible if a background refresh fails, and re-running keeps the page populated.

highlights.text: Phase-based loading checklist with structured progress (scan/price/insights) and percent meter instead of per-file spam
Instant open shows the last saved report while a fresh run loads in the background with a banner showing phase and progress
Failed refresh keeps the stale report visible with an error notice; re-running refreshes the report without losing your place
Progress events are throttled and folded per phase — a 737-file scan now shows one meter instead of 737 lines

entries.summary: The standup page now renders each team member's work as a Jira-style story-centered member card with issue hierarchy. Your main user story becomes the visible unit of each card, with subtasks nested underneath and a status lozenge showing progress. The redesign supports both Jira and Azure DevOps hierarchy, automatically detecting issue types and parent-child relationships without extra API calls. Code and documentation changes are now filed under their referencing story, and legacy reports render unchanged for backward compatibility.

highlights.text: Story-centered member cards with Jira-style issue hierarchy — main story is the visible unit with subtasks nested underneath
Status lozenges show progress (TO DO / IN PROGRESS / DONE / BLOCKED) with audited palette colors across all themes
Automatic hierarchy detection for Jira and Azure DevOps — no extra API calls, works with team-managed stories and all process templates
Code and documentation changes filed under their referencing story, with exact-reference attachment — orphaned work stays visible

entries.summary: yeaboi now covers agents, not just humans. After the splash you pick who we're working with today: Humans (the duck, and every existing mode) or Agents (a new robotic duck, and a new family of modes that watch the AI agents working across your SDLC). The first three agent modes ship in beta: Usage prices your local Claude Code sessions per model, project and day; Standup digests what your agents did — sessions worked plus agent-authored commits and PRs found in your trackers; Security audits your agent setup — permission bypasses, wildcard allows, risky hooks, MCP servers, and secret exposure in transcripts, reported as pattern+file+line only. Everything is computed locally from your own session logs; transcripts are never copied, uploaded or stored. Full parity from day one: every agent mode has a CLI subcommand (yeaboi agents ...), MCP tools, and a plugin skill. The existing Usage page's cost estimate now uses a real per-model pricing table instead of a flat Sonnet rate, so displayed costs may shift.

highlights.text: Humans/Agents landing split with a robotic duck for the new family
Agents → Usage: per-model/project/day cost of your local agent sessions, cache-aware pricing
Agents → Standup: daily digest of agent sessions + agent-authored commits/PRs, Slack-deliverable
Agents → Security: settings/MCP/secret audit of your agent setup (indicator, not an audit)
yeaboi agents cost|standup|security CLI + six new MCP tools + three plugin skills
Usage page cost estimates now use per-model rates (numbers may shift from the old flat estimate)

entries.summary: Demo GIF recording is now deterministic, repeatable, and verified — glyph corruption from multibyte characters is structurally impossible, and terminal size, keystroke timing, and environment are hermetic. A new YEABOI_UPDATE_CHECK environment variable lets you disable the background PyPI update check, which is essential for air-gapped systems and prevents the version row from repainting during captures. The recording script includes built-in verification that fails loudly on blank frames, missing artifacts, or oversize GIFs.

highlights.text: YEABOI_UPDATE_CHECK environment variable: disable the background PyPI update check for air-gapped installs
Deterministic demo GIF recording: make demo re-records and verifies in ~13 seconds with no variation between runs
Built-in verification gates: recording fails loudly on blank frames, missing artifacts, or oversize output
make demo-render re-renders from the committed cast without re-recording, for theme or size tweaks

entries.summary: Major version: the OpenClaw integration (the shipped `skills/` package and `--install-skill` CLI flag) is removed entirely. This surfaces the true nature of yeaboi as a standalone terminal agent, not an OpenClaw plugin. The app focuses now on six surfaces: the TUI, CLI flags/subcommands, the Python engines, the MCP server, the Claude Code plugin skills, and the live-board REST API — OpenClaw itself lives only in historical changelog entries. Unused tree bloat (700+ accidentally-committed node_modules files, orphaned docs, and design packages) is also removed.

highlights.text: OpenClaw integration removed: no `--install-skill` flag, no `src/yeaboi/skills/` shipped plugin, no Bedrock auto-detect sandbox
Surface parity updated: five surfaces now (down from six) — TUI, CLI, Python engines, MCP server, Claude Code plugin
Tree cleanup: removed ~700 node_modules files from desktop-pet/, orphaned screenshots, design packages, and legacy docs

entries.summary: Double-tapping Space now installs dictation automatically if the voice packages are missing — no need to reinstall yeaboi with the `voice` extra or restart. The in-app offer lets you Enter to install and download the Whisper model with a real progress bar, Esc to skip for this session, or `n` to never ask again. The install happens instantly in the running app, ready to record right away. A headless `--install-voice` command brings the same feature to CI containers and headless terminals with plain output that survives piping. Every surface now renders voice readiness from one shared vocabulary — `ready`, `installable`, `declined`, or `unsupported` — so the input chip, welcome tip, settings row, and setup wizard always agree about the same machine.

highlights.text: In-app voice installation: double-tap Space opens an offer to install and download Whisper model with progress bar
Choose Enter to install, Esc to skip this session, or n to never ask again — sticky per-machine verdicts
Installs directly into the running interpreter, downloads the Whisper model with real byte-percentage progress, ready to record
`yeaboi --install-voice` headless command for CI, containers, and terminals where full-screen UI can't run
One shared voice_state() vocabulary: ready/installable/declined/unsupported renders consistently across all surfaces

entries.summary: The in-app `ctrl+U` upgrade now seamlessly restarts the app onto the newly installed version, preserving CLI flags like `--dry-run` and `--theme` so you stay where you were. The upgrade screen counts down 3 seconds and relaunches automatically, or press Esc/Q to decline and stay on the current version. The restarted app skips the splash animation and shows a `✓ updated` confirmation on the version row. Honest fallbacks appear if the upgrade fails, the restart can't be resolved, or you're on a non-POSIX system.

highlights.text: Seamless self-restart after upgrade: auto-relaunch in 3s onto the new version with Esc to decline
Preserved context: CLI flags like --dry-run, --theme stay active through the restart
Confirmation chip: ✓ updated appears on the version row after a successful restart
Honest fallbacks: upgrade failures and restart impossibilities show the old "restart manually" screen

entries.summary: Planning mode got eight quality-of-life improvements that speed up intake and make the chat feel more responsive. Type a digit (1/2/3) to instantly pick and submit on size and review choices, no Enter needed — the feature even works on multi-choice rows. The progress subtitle now reads "Question X of Y" over the set this run actually asks (not the full question bank), and a new `/questions` command lists planned topics with status markers. Large responses (intake summaries, review walls) skip the fake typewriter effect and land directly as artifact cards. The review verdict is now a selectable row — Accept / Edit an answer / Override velocity / Tell me what's off — mapped to node literals so digits and raw text never reach the graph. A clock-derived duck quip rotates every 5 seconds of a long wait, with a quack every fourth slot and one shades gag on really long ones. Small projects are hard-capped at 2 stories total and trimmed post-validate with a warning. Fast mode gained a visible subtitle and an `/finish` toggle to auto-accept remaining questions and exit the chat.

highlights.text: Bare digit auto-submit: 1/2/3 picks and submits on size/review rows, no Enter needed
Honest question count: subtitle shows "Question X of Y" over only the questions this run asks
/questions command lists planned topics with ✓/●/○ markers
No wall-of-text streaming: large deterministic replies (intake summary, review walls) land directly as artifact cards
Selectable review verdict: Accept / Edit an answer / Override velocity / Tell me what's off choice rows
Duck entertainment: clock-derived quip rotator every 5s of a wait, with a quack every fourth slot and one shades gag on long waits
Small projects hard-capped at 2 stories total, with post-validate trim and warning
Fast mode visible exit: "Fast mode (Esc stops)" subtitle, /finish toggle to auto-accept and exit the chat

entries.summary: Voice input now lets you pick which microphone to use, making it work on hardware that wasn't detected before. Most USB and Bluetooth mics refuse to open at Whisper's default 16 kHz mono format — voice input now negotiates whatever format your mic actually supports, records natively, and converts afterward, so audio gets captured even on finicky hardware. A new Settings page lets you test each microphone, and Tab during recording switches between them on the fly. The feature is now discoverable in the TUI with an input-level meter and "no sound detected" warning, plus a new `--list-audio-devices` CLI diagnostic.

highlights.text: VOICE_DEVICE config option: pick a microphone by PortAudio index or name substring
Settings → Voice Input → Input Device: new picker with live microphone test
Tab to switch microphones mid-recording, with device name and input-level meter
Format negotiation: records at the microphone's native sample rate and channels, then resamples to Whisper format
`--list-audio-devices` CLI subcommand to discover available microphones and test the audio input
"No sound reaching the mic" warning and better affordance positioning for voice hints

entries.summary: Fixed standup mode's Generate command failing with "no such column: origin" error. The issue was caused by a schema version collision in the session database — a migration that added edit-provenance tracking (`origin` column) was skipped due to version numbering conflicts, but code continued to query for those columns. The fix re-applies the missing migration idempotently, hardens the schema version tracking to prevent duplicates, and adds self-healing to all standalone mode stores so they can repair their own tables on opening.

highlights.text: Fixed standup Generate command crashing with "no such column: origin" error
Database schema repairs are now idempotent and self-healing across all mode stores
Session database schema version tracking deduplicated and race-guarded to prevent future collisions

entries.summary: Fixed planning mode's live chat asking about project size twice. The greeting's small-vs-large answer now properly flows through the chat, with mode-aware lead-ins for follow-up questions that acknowledge the earlier choice. Smart mode chat also hides the redundant sprint-count row that only appears for large projects.

highlights.text: Fixed chat asking project size twice: mode-aware lead-ins now acknowledge the greeting answer
Redundant option filtering: smart mode hides the 1–2 sprints row that only applies to large projects

entries.summary: The idle screensaver expanded from a single duck to a yard of them — ten-odd heads adrift in zero gravity, spinning and ricocheting off each other and an anchored duck in the middle. The screensaver activates with Ctrl+Y as before, and still reads as a single resting duck on terminals smaller than 60x24, so the existing single-duck graphics cover those smaller screens.

highlights.text: Idle screensaver now shows a yard of ricocheting ducks with pixel-perfect collisions and real rotation
Ducks bounce off each other and the frame edges with squash physics; anchored hero duck in the center never moves
Sprite rotation is memoised with 48 angles and 5 squash levels for smooth performance

entries.summary: The planning duck is now the TUI's living mascot across every mode. He waddles into the corner whenever you enter a mode, head-bobs through every long wait (standups, 1:1s, reports, syncs, shares), and quacks a short quip when those operations complete. A sticky rubber-duck tier serves hidden confirmations — delete prompts are now unmissable even on narrow terminals, and the bubble lane stays off the right edge so your composer never overlaps with encouragement. The shared loading screens gained live progress: a braille spinner, per-stage elapsed timing, and a [n/total] footer. Retro action drafting, performance 1:1 generation, and Notion/Confluence publishing no longer freeze the screen — they run on background workers with a live busy affordance. The duck is mutable per-session via /duck in the chat, and globally via the new Duck row in Settings → System.

highlights.text: Living mascot: the duck waddles in when you open a mode and head-bobs through every long wait
Completion quips: duck quacks a short reactive message when standups, reports, syncs, shares, or analysis exports finish
Unfrozen waits: retro action drafting, performance 1:1 generation, and Notion/Confluence publishing run on workers with live progress instead of freezing
Sticky confirmations: delete prompts and other critical modals now show as a sticky duck tier, unmissable even below 97 columns
Live progress meters: loading screens show a braille spinner, per-stage elapsed time, and [n/total] footer; planning chat shows a full build checklist with recap card
Duck mute control: /duck in planning chat or Settings → System → Duck row; persisted per-user via DUCK_ENABLED

entries.summary: Fixed share links from retro and poker boards serving Cloudflare errors forever. Tunnel readiness now verifies that cloudflared has fully registered with the edge (not just started up and printed its URL), and recovers automatically if the regional DNS lookup fails by retrying with a pinned US region. Cancelling a board session now cleanly stops any in-flight tunnel startup, preventing orphaned processes.

highlights.text: Share links now wait for tunnel to register with Cloudflare edge before advertising the URL
Regional DNS lookup failures automatically retry with --region us, unblocking resolvers that answer incomplete SRV records
Cancelled board sessions now cleanly stop tunnel startup, preventing orphaned processes

entries.summary: Planning mode is now a continuous live chat instead of a card-based questionnaire. Type naturally, and the agent streams its thoughts while it gathers your project goals, team shape, and delivery timeline. Slash commands (type `/help` mid-draft) let you skip questions, reset to defaults, switch to the classic form, or wrap up fast with `/finish`. Watch artifact cards — epics, features, stories, tasks, sprints — render in the transcript as they're drafted. New projects can pick Small or Large at the start, or just describe your project and let the classifier decide. The chat stays in sync with the headless engine, so exports and platform partners see the same project shape.

highlights.text: Planning mode is now a continuous live chat that streams agent thoughts as it gathers project details
Slash commands (`/help`, `/skip`, `/finish`, `/form`, `/edit`, `/export` and more) for mid-draft control without typing the full response
Watch epics, features, stories, tasks and sprints render as cards in the transcript while the agent drafts them
Choose project size up-front (Small/Large) or describe your project and let the classifier size it
Chat and form modes are swappable mid-intake, and `/finish` auto-accepts all remaining questions for a fast path through the pipeline

The corner duck is now the TUI's experience layer: he head-bobs through every long wait, quacks a short quip when a standup, report, analysis, export, sync or share link completes, and waddles into the corner whenever you open a mode
Loading screens gained a live checklist — braille spinner, per-stage elapsed and a [n/total] progress footer — and the planning chat shows a full build checklist with a completion recap card
Duck bubble mute: /duck in the planning chat or the new Duck row in Settings → System (persisted as DUCK_ENABLED); delete confirmations stay visible regardless
Retro action-item drafting, performance 1:1 generation and Notion/Confluence publishing no longer freeze the screen — they run on workers with live progress

entries.summary: Analysis mode now discovers and offers GitHub as a code source in the setup wizard — owners, organizations, and repositories are discovered automatically, and the choice is saved to Settings for future runs. GitHub was technically supported all along but gated behind a configuration key that had no UI surface; now it reaches parity with Azure DevOps, which was always offered once connected.

highlights.text: GitHub is now discoverable and selectable in the Analysis setup wizard, on equal footing with Azure DevOps
GitHub owners and organizations are discovered automatically from the configured token, no manual entry needed
Chosen GitHub owners persist in Settings → GitHub → Analysis Owners for future runs and CLI commands
Fine-grained GitHub PATs now work with Analysis — even if they cannot list organizations, the picker will find them via visible repositories

entries.summary: Daily Standup now flags engineering practices that might cost your team later — work that lands with no ticket, a board left stale after a merge, too many changes open at once, or changes too big to review. Seven deterministic rules catch these patterns per team member, capped at three signals each. Every signal names the exact changes it observed — no LLM is involved in detection. Wrong calls are answered: teammates can thumbs-down to hide a signal and it remembers; thumbs-up confirms it. Answers appear in the TUI, over MCP, and in the shared HTML page where the teammate reading it usually spots the mistake first.

highlights.text: Standup now detects engineering bad habits: untracked work, stale boards, too many open changes, and commits too big to review
Each signal names the exact changes it observed, with no LLM judgment involved
Teammates can thumbs-down a signal to hide it or thumbs-up to confirm it's correct
Signals are voteable in three places: the TUI member detail, the shared HTML page, and over the MCP standup_practice_feedback tool
An optional LLM pass can catch untracked work that was mentioned in a ticket without linking it

entries.summary: Daily Standup now asks for the meeting transcript instead of waiting for one. Paste it from your clipboard, pipe it in, drag the file across, or point Standup at the folder your recordings already land in — Zoom, Google Meet and Downloads are detected and offered by name. When a standup runs and no transcript is ever checked against it, Standup says so: quietly at first, in the terminal only, and after several in a row it offers to turn the feature off rather than keep asking. An optional reminder can arrive shortly after your standup, and only when something is actually unchecked.

highlights.text: Paste, pipe or drag a standup transcript in — no more finding the right folder first
Your Zoom, Google Meet and Downloads folders are detected and offered by name, with a count and the newest date
Standups that were never checked against their meeting are now surfaced, escalating to an offer to switch the feature off
An optional desktop reminder 30 minutes to 2 hours after the standup, which stays silent when nothing is unchecked
The transcript folder and the automatic pre-standup review are now settable in the terminal app, not only over MCP

entries.summary: Every shared artifact — your standup, retrospective, or report — is now editable by teammates who have the link. When the standup gets your work wrong, the person reading it can fix the text right there: correct a misspelled blocker, append something the scan missed, or add a note nobody thought to include. Every change is attributed to a self-declared name and can be reverted, and the corrected text becomes the version that exports, feeds into history, and reaches the next day's standup so the team doesn't repeat the same mistakes. Editing works through the browser; nothing needs to be re-run.

highlights.text: Teammates can now correct and edit shared standups, reports and retrospectives directly from the shared link
Every correction is attributed to a self-declared name, timestamped and can be reverted
Corrected text feeds forward to the next run so mistakes aren't repeated
Edit history shows what changed and who changed it, with timestamps
All edits are made through the browser — standups and reports are never re-run

entries.summary: Daily Standup no longer walks you through five pickers on every run — tracker sources, team members, code sources, repositories, and documentation sources — when you've already told it once. Generate now opens with a summary of your saved setup and three buttons: Use Saved goes straight to "Your update for today", Change lets you adjust any settings (still pre-selected from last time), and Back cancels. The gate only appears when there's something to reuse; first runs and incomplete setups are unchanged.

highlights.text: Standup Generate offers your saved setup on every run: Use Saved, Change, or Back
The summary shows your configured trackers, team, code sources, and docs without scrolling
Saved selections are still pre-selected if you choose Change, and are self-healed if an integration is removed

entries.summary: Copying an invite link now gives you one working URL instead of a broken two-line clipboard payload. Teammates clicking a stale link now get a clear "That invite link is out of date" message instead of a confusing error, and the code is preserved in the URL fragment so it stays out of server logs and referer headers. The fix applies to both live retro and planning poker boards and Share Online exports across all modes.

highlights.text: Invite links now carry the access code in the URL fragment, making them a single working link
Stale links show a clear message and don't spam failed join attempts to the server
Applies to both live boards and Share Online exports
Fixed: Copy Invite button produced a broken two-line payload that failed when pasted into address bars or chat

entries.summary: Everything yeaboi puts in a browser now looks like the same product. The live retro and planning poker boards, the page that asks for a share code, the reports you export and the slide deck had each drifted into their own look — different headers, different buttons, and a colour theme that only applied where you happened to pick it. They now share one design: the same header carrying the mode's name and colour, the same footer, and a theme you choose anywhere that follows you everywhere, including the next report you export. The slide deck gains a light mode and prints properly for the first time. A share link's page now says what kind of thing is waiting behind it — “a standup”, “a retro” — so the person you sent it to knows what they are joining before they type the code; the one exception is Performance, which stays deliberately anonymous, because naming it would tell whoever holds the link that somebody's 1:1 or review is behind the door. Live boards are also served with the same security headers as every other page, browser tabs now name the session instead of reading “Sprint Retro” on every one of them, and a ceremony timer that could stick on one second now counts down properly.

highlights.text: Boards, share pages, exported reports and the slide deck all wear the same header, footer and colours
A theme picked on one surface now follows you to the others, and to the next report you export
The slide deck gains a light mode and finally prints correctly
A share page names what is behind it — except Performance, which stays anonymous on purpose
Live boards are served with the same security headers and content policy as every other page
Browser tabs name the session, so three open boards are no longer three identical tabs
Fixed: the shared countdown timer could stick on one second instead of counting down

entries.summary: Performance mode is now clearly marked as beta wherever you meet it. The mode works exactly as before and nothing has been taken away — but its 1:1 preps, completion summaries and six-month reviews have not yet been checked against a real team's delivery data, and until now nothing on screen said so. That matters more here than elsewhere, because these drafts are about named people. The Performance card on the welcome screen and the page header both carry a BETA tag, and the first time you open the mode you get a short one-time note explaining what is and isn't reliable: the drafts are a starting point rather than an assessment, a board with little on it produces thin and sometimes misleading signals, and nothing is emailed to anyone unless you ask for it. You will only see that note once. The same caveat now appears when you use Performance from the command line or through an AI assistant.

highlights.text: Performance is labelled BETA on the mode card and page header — the mode stays fully usable
A one-time notice on first entry explains what the drafts can and can't tell you, and that nothing is sent automatically
The same beta caveat now reaches the command line and AI-assistant integrations, not just the app
Beta notices can be silenced for scripted runs, and replayed on demand for demos

entries.summary: Inviting people to a live retro or planning poker board is now one link that works for everyone, wherever they are. Boards used to offer a link that only worked for teammates on the same Wi-Fi, with a separate “Share Remotely” button to add an internet-reachable one on top — and it was easy to send the wrong one to someone at home. Every board now sets up a single secure link by itself the moment it opens, and that is the link Copy Invite gives you. The board is also no longer reachable from your local network at all, so it is not exposed to everyone else on an office or café connection, and your own host link travels encrypted. Two things to know: hosting a board now needs an internet connection, and the invite link takes a few seconds to appear while it is being prepared — the access code works straight away.

highlights.text: One secure link per board, set up automatically — the separate “Share Remotely” step is gone
Copy Invite and Copy Host Link always give the link that works for everyone, never a local-network address
Boards are no longer reachable from your local network, so they aren't exposed on shared Wi-Fi
Hosting a board now needs an internet connection; the invite link appears a few seconds after the board opens

entries.summary: Every page yeaboi opens in a browser — the retro board, planning poker, the join screen and the reporting slide deck — has been rebuilt on one shared design, so they now read as parts of the same app rather than three pages that had quietly drifted apart. Inviting people got easier: both live boards hand you a copyable invite link, and you can copy it from the terminal too instead of only holding up a QR code. The retro board gains a composer at the top of every column and sixteen reactions to vote with, and dragging a card on a phone finally works — touch dragging never fired at all before. Planning poker's reveal is a moment now rather than a flicker, and the timer ends on a bell instead of an alarm. Boards also stay current without the constant one-second refresh, which is gentler on a phone battery and on a shared tunnel. Every exported HTML report is drawn by the same pieces as the live boards, so an export matches what you saw. One fix worth naming: a ticket link in an export could previously carry a script that ran when you clicked it, and can't any more.

highlights.text: The retro board, planning poker, the join screen and the slide deck rebuilt on one shared design
Copy a board's invite link from the browser or from the terminal, instead of only scanning the QR code
A composer at the top of every retro column, and sixteen reactions to vote with
Cards can be dragged on a phone — touch dragging did not work before
A ticket link in an exported report can no longer run a script when clicked

entries.summary: The welcome screen gains a duck companion who now does more than sit there: press f and a speech bubble opens from him that you write your feedback straight into, pick a type and area for, paste screenshots into, or dictate out loud. Settings gets a full rebuild around boxed sections you can drive entirely from the keyboard — arrow between boxes, Enter to focus one, then arrow between the values inside it — with storage settings moved under System and long status lines that wrap instead of getting cut off. Clicking now works across the whole app rather than just the main menu, and a handful of small annoyances are gone: the Back button leaves in one click, the controls drawer opens with c, and the wordmark intro no longer replays every time you open Changelog, Feedback, or All Tips.

highlights.text: Write and send feedback in a speech bubble from the duck, with image paste and voice dictation
Settings laid out as boxed sections you can navigate and edit with the keyboard alone
Storage settings moved under System, and long status lines wrap instead of truncating
Clicking buttons, rows, and cards now works on every screen, not just the main menu
Back leaves in one click, c opens the controls drawer, and the intro animation no longer replays on secondary pages

entries.summary: Reporting mode reaches feature and UX parity with Analysis and Standup with six major capability launches. Threaded generation runs the engine on a background worker behind a shared progress screen with full cancellation support, and adds Last Week and custom date range periods with automatic window clamping for delivered items. The new theme registry (4 built-in themes plus custom palettes from ~/.yeaboi/data/reporting_themes.json) flows into HTML deck CSS, .pptx slides, CLI --theme flag, and MCP tools. Native .pptx export now available as an optional docs extra with graceful degradation if python-pptx is missing. Per-component source selection (delivery/code/docs) lets you pick what gets included, and deterministic supporting signals (merged PRs, commits, doc updates) appear as bounded reference-only rows with corroboration footnotes. Persisted DeckStyle preferences control title/heading colors, font presets, layout density, bullets, section toggles, and slide numbers with neutral defaults. New layout.py planner delivers content-aware slide packing shared by both renderers: full-width lone cards, greedy 2-column layouts, pagination with (cont.) markers, and a content_fit mode (ask/expand/tight) that lets users decide whether to add slides when content exceeds bounds. Visual quality improvements include top-anchored outcome cards, height-fitted delivered-items table with explicit column widths, deduplicated items (collapsed ticket + changelog rows), executive summary as sentence bullets, and flattened doc-collector progress. Packaged pixel-duck mark appears on both surfaces (inline data URI, offline-safe).

highlights.text: Threaded generation with background worker, live progress screen, and Esc cancellation; Last Week and custom date range periods added
Theme registry: 4 built-in themes + custom palettes from ~/.yeaboi/data/reporting_themes.json flowing into HTML, .pptx, CLI, and MCP
Native .pptx export via python-pptx (optional docs extra); gracefully degrades to HTML if missing
Per-component source selection (delivery/code/docs); deterministic supporting signals as bounded reference rows with corroboration footnotes
Persisted DeckStyle preferences: colors, fonts, layout density, section toggles, slide numbers; content-aware slide packing with ask/expand/tight fit modes

entries.summary: Daily Standup unlocked six major capabilities that transform how standups work: automated scheduling (set it and run headless), intelligent day-over-day insights (blockers, progress signals, outlook), humanized export cards with ticket links and activity bars, automation detection (bots and scanners excluded from credit), and theme-aware visualizations across all eight modes. The export redesign landed per-member cards instead of tables, readable bullets with hanging indent, theme-aware sparklines and progress bars, and avatar chips. Then the visual system rolled out to Retro, Poker, Performance, Reporting, and Roadmap exports with the same polish.

highlights.text: Schedule wizard: set time, lead, weekdays, and channels; runs scheduled standups headless via launchd/cron
Day-over-day intelligence: blocker detection, previous-day progress notes, AI-written outlook, trend-aware confidence with delta fields
HTML/Markdown redesign: per-member cards with ticket links, readable sentence-split bullets, badge-chip links, adaptive grid, coverage dots
Automation detection: filter out bot and scanner comments via content markers and metadata; always surface as Notices
Theme-aware visual system: sparklines, segment bars, avatars, legends, progress bars in all five themes + print across Standup/Retro/Poker/Performance/Reporting

entries.summary: Security-hardened release elevating the app's trust foundation across five independent workstreams. A new filesystem sandbox restricts all reads and writes to ~/.yeaboi unless explicitly allowed, with interactive TUI consent and Settings integration. Sensitive credentials and tokens are now redacted from all logs and tracebacks. Every external write tool (Jira/Azure DevOps ticket creation) now requires human confirmation before executing. HTML exports were hardened against XSS injection across all eight exporters with consolidated escaping. File permissions were tightened (chmod 0o600 for logs and database), and a non-blocking CodeQL workflow adds continuous static analysis. Manual end-to-end testing confirms sandbox denial paths work, and all existing functionality remains backward-compatible.

highlights.text: New filesystem sandbox: restricts all reads/writes to ~/.yeaboi unless explicitly allowed via Settings, --allow-path flag, or YEABOI_ALLOWED_PATHS env var
Interactive TUI consent flow for path access: Allow once / Always allow / Deny, with post-turn retry queue
Secret redaction in all logs: automatic scrubbing of env secrets and token shapes from messages and tracebacks
Full write-tool gating: ticket creation tools now require human confirmation before executing
HTML export XSS hardening: consolidated escaping, real-leak fixes across all eight exporters, and probe-injection harness

entries.summary: Every TUI screen now displays with its mode's signature background color — a dark tint of the accent (analysis green, planning blue, standup magenta, retro teal, poker gold, performance rust, reporting violet, usage amber) instead of your terminal's default, ensuring the app looks identical and polished across any terminal theme. Home, splash, provider select, settings, changelog, and feedback use a neutral dark base. The change includes a shared root-panel helper, full-screen AST guards to prevent regressions, and new truecolor rendering tests.

highlights.text: Every mode-specific TUI screen now displays with its mode's background tint for a polished, consistent look
Neutral dark base for home, splash, settings, and other cross-mode screens
Appearance is now identical across all terminal themes thanks to baked-in backgrounds
New AST guard + truecolor tests prevent raw full-screen Panels from merging in the future

entries.summary: Team analysis evolved into a comprehensive, member-scoped investigation of how your team works. The AI Usage card now leads with an engineering-practices table scoring tests-with-changes, documentation clarity, ticket references, and PR description quality across all attributed work — honest denominators, small-sample transparency, and a recomputed team row. The same table appears in markdown and HTML exports. Performance overhaul adds pooled tracker fetching, a schema v19 model-keyed analysis cache, cold-run lookup caps with disclosed truncation, activity-targeted repo scanning, and fan-out dedup. Scope controls let you pick sources per component (delivery reads Jira/Azure DevOps, code scans GitHub/Azure Repos, docs reads Confluence/Notion), pick specific members, run dual-source analyses, and persist analysis features per run. Doc quality now reads page content for clarity and AI usage estimates with evidence links. Default analysis depth is now `deep` on all surfaces. UX gains include wizard Esc back-stepping, Ctrl-C cooperative cancel, AzDO SDK clients pinned to the configured org URL, and render-side caps preventing oversized tables from rendering blank.

highlights.text: AI Usage card redesigned: per-member practices table (tests, docs, tickets, PR quality) replacing simple footprint
Member-scoped analysis with explicit source selection and dual-source runs (Jira + Azure DevOps together)
Doc quality reads page content for clarity + AI-usage estimates with evidence links
Performance overhaul: pooled fetching, analysis cache (v19), lookup caps with transparent truncation, activity-targeted scanning
Default analysis depth is now `deep` on all surfaces; scope controls, feature selection, and render-side caps prevent blank viewports

entries.summary: All shareable HTML exports now share a cohesive, polished design system. Every mode's export page — planning, standup, retro, performance, reporting, roadmap, team profile, and anonymize — uses unified five-theme palettes (midnight, light, solarized, synthwave, forest) with a persistent theme switcher. A self-contained header button cycles themes and remembers your choice in localStorage; printing always forces light tokens. New semantic color tokens (`--ok`, `--warn`, `--danger`, priority ramps, text variants) replace scattered hardcoded hex values across eight exporters, and shared page chrome primitives (`html_page()`, `chip()`, `section()`, `stat_tile()`, `stat_bar()`, `notice_block()`) unify markup and reduce duplication. The design is self-contained with no external CDN or requests. Incidentally fixes an unstyled container in the anonymize export and corrects four double-escaped ampersands in team-profile titles.

highlights.text: Five unified theme palettes (midnight default, light, solarized, synthwave, forest) across all eight export pages
Persistent theme switcher in a header button; localStorage remembers choice and printing forces light tokens
Shared semantic color tokens and page chrome primitives reduce duplication across exporters
Self-contained design with no CDN or external requests; all resources inline
Bug fixes: unstyled anonymize export container and corrected double-escaped ampersands in team profile

entries.summary: Daily Standup activity coverage got a major upgrade with explicit source selection before generation. Before standup runs, you now pick which trackers (Jira, Azure DevOps), repositories (GitHub, Azure Repos), and documentation (Confluence, Notion) to scan — letting you focus the report on what matters. Member updates are split into source-specific summaries with evidence links: your GitHub PR activity shows up separately from Jira work, which appears distinct from Confluence pages you edited. The app collects all sources in parallel for speed, caches metadata, and surfaces live progress with partial-coverage notices when some sources aren't configured. Results display as responsive Analysis-style dashboards showing each team member's activity across all sources, and saved-run rendering stays consistent when you re-open a historical standup.

highlights.text: Explicit source selection grid before standup generation — pick trackers, repos, and docs to scan
Member updates split by source with separate summaries and evidence links for each tracker, repo, and docs platform
Parallel source collection with live progress and partial-coverage notices
Metadata caching and bounded network work for faster, more reliable runs
Redesigned results as responsive Analysis-style dashboards; saved runs render identically when reopened

entries.summary: Team analysis now offers two speed tiers. Quick mode runs instantly with deterministic summaries and no LLM calls—perfect for fast iterations during planning sessions. Deep mode activates AI-enriched analysis with larger ticket batches and parallel processing of all three analysis components (delivery, code, and documentation) for comprehensive insights. The Quick/Deep choice appears right before analysis starts in both the TUI workflow and CLI, with mode details and stage timings visible throughout the run. All three components now run concurrently instead of serially, cutting analysis wall-clock time significantly. The choice is exposed through CLI flags and MCP tools so teammates and AI agents can pick the right depth for their workflow.

highlights.text: Quick mode: instant, deterministic analysis with no LLM calls; perfect for fast iterations
Deep mode: AI-enriched with larger ticket batches and parallel processing of delivery, code, and docs components
Choose Quick or Deep right before analysis starts; mode details and stage timings shown during the run
Concurrent component analysis cuts wall-clock time; delivery, code, and documentation run in parallel
Analysis depth exposed through CLI flags and MCP tools for programmatic control

entries.summary: Analysis mode gained significantly improved insights dashboards. AI Adoption and Documentation sections now display as evidence-led dashboards with metric tiles, meters, ranked member breakdowns, evidence tables, and actionable cards — replacing a flat text layout with data-forward visualization. Team Insights was reorganized into consistent Focus Now, Keep Working, and Experiments sections, each with category badges for quick scanning. Member selection was redesigned: every team member starts pre-selected in the analysis scope picker, you can toggle one at a time or press A to select or deselect all, and the app prevents running with nobody selected. Overall scrolling and navigation improved for better usability with rich content.

highlights.text: Redesigned AI Adoption and Documentation as data-driven dashboards with metrics, breakdowns, evidence tables, and actions
Team Insights reorganized into Focus Now, Keep Working, and Experiments with category badges
Member selection pre-selects everyone; toggle individual members or press A to select/deselect all; prevents running with nobody selected
